_comment: QR-login status polling (/api/v1/auth/qr/status/*) - carved out of teezer-auth's 30/60s IP cap. This endpoint is polled every 3s by design (login-content.tsx's QR_POLL_MS / QrLoginController::status()) and is keyed on an opaque, unguessable, 2-minute ticket id, not an account - the strict tier's budget exists for credential-stuffing-sensitive routes (login/OTP/2FA). Normal polling alone is ~20 req/min, which left almost no headroom under teezer-auth's shared 30/60s IP cap for the initial qr/create call or any other auth activity on the same IP within the same 60s window - real users saw 'This code has expired' + a 429 toast within seconds of opening the QR modal, not because the ticket had actually expired but because qrCreate()/subsequent polls were being rejected by APISIX before ever reaching Laravel. Laravel's own qr-login-status limiter (40/min, keyed per-ticket, AppServiceProvider.php) is still the real per-ticket abuse guard underneath this - this route only widens the blunt IP-wide gate for this one legitimately-chatty path. qr/create itself stays under the original teezer-auth strict tier (priority 10) - it's called once per attempt, not polled, so the strict budget is still appropriate there. Added 2026-08-25. Brought into git 2026-09-03: it had been applied by hand and existed only on VPS1 (root-owned, mode 600), so a gateway rebuild would have silently dropped it and QR login would have started 429ing under teezer-auth's strict tier again. It was also the last route still counting with policy: local.
name: teezer-auth-qr-status
desc: QR-login status polling - carved out of teezer-auth's 30/60s IP cap, which real 3s polling was exhausting alone (see /home/ubuntu/config-changes/apisix-routes/07-auth-qr-status.json for the full comment).
